name: Soho Grand Hotel
positioning: Independent boutique hotel on West Broadway, opened in 1996 as SoHo's first luxury boutique hotel, with Bill Sofield interiors that nod to the neighborhood's industrial past
best_for: Travelers who want a design-minded base between SoHo and Tribeca
Couples who want a terrace suite or penthouse loft with Manhattan views

facts.text: Soho Grand sits on a quiet West Broadway block straddling SoHo and Tribeca.
The hotel stands seventeen stories tall, and most windows frame a view of Downtown Manhattan.
The hotel's interiors were designed by Bill Sofield.
Guest rooms blend design elements from the mid-century to the late Seventies.
In 2019 the hotel underwent a full renovation that added terrace suites and updated bedroom interiors.
The Loft South Penthouse pays homage to SoHo's 1970s artist lofts.
The Terrace Suite has a private terrace with an outdoor shower.
A dog park around the corner on Grand Street is available to guests.
Pet bowls, beds and crates are available on request.
The Club Room is the hotel's cocktail bar with live jazz.
The Grand Bar and Salon offers a selection of 50 rare American whiskeys.
The fitness center on the third floor is open 24 hours.

highlights.text: Soho Grand opened in 1996 as SoHo's first luxury boutique hotel.
The design nods to SoHo's industrial heritage with a staircase lit by bottle glass, cast-iron molding and masonry columns.
The Loft North Penthouse has two bedrooms, a separate living room, a full-service cocktail bar and panoramic views of the Empire State Building.
The hotel is especially pet friendly, with cast-iron dog sculptures throughout its lobby.
The fitness center on the third floor has a balcony suited to morning yoga.

considerations.text: Gilligan's, the open-air, palm-treed beach bar, is open only from May through late September.
WhataHotel notes typical city noise levels in this urban location.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the Manhattan location.
